faqs.a: You need a recognised university degree, a concrete job offer or signed contract in Germany lasting at least six months, and a gross salary that meets the 2026 threshold: €50,700 a year for most roles, or €45,934.20 for shortage occupations and recent graduates.
faqs.q: What are the requirements for the EU Blue Card in Germany?

faqs.a: The standard threshold for 2026 is €50,700 gross a year, which is €4,225 a month. A reduced threshold of €45,934.20 a year applies to shortage occupations such as MINT fields, medicine and IT, to graduates from the last three years, and to qualifying IT specialists without a degree.
faqs.q: What is the EU Blue Card salary threshold for 2026?

faqs.a: Yes. IT specialists with at least three years of professional IT experience within the last seven years, at a level comparable to a degree, can qualify under section 18g(2) of the Residence Act. The reduced threshold of €45,934.20 applies, and Federal Employment Agency approval is required.
faqs.q: Can I get a Blue Card without a university degree?

faqs.a: The Blue Card can lead to settlement after 27 months, or after 21 months if you hold B1-level German. The official processing time is generally 4 to 12 weeks. The visa fee is €75 and the residence title costs €100, with a ZAB Statement of Comparability costing €208 when needed.

headline: Germany EU Blue Card Requirements 2026: Salary, Degree and Application
metaDescription: Germany EU Blue Card 2026: standard threshold €50,700, reduced €45,934.20 for shortage jobs, degree rules, IT route without a degree, settlement in 27 months.

sections.content:
The EU Blue Card is Germany's residence permit for highly qualified non-EU professionals under section 18g of the Residence Act. It combines a work and residence permit in one document and offers a faster route to settlement than the general skilled worker permit.

To qualify you need a recognised university degree, a concrete job offer or signed contract lasting at least six months, and a salary that meets the official threshold. The Blue Card is tied to your job at first, but it gives you mobility across the EU after 18 months.
sections.title: What is the EU Blue Card?

sections.content:
In 2026 the standard threshold is €50,700 gross a year, or €4,225 a month, and at this salary no Federal Employment Agency approval is needed. A reduced threshold of €45,934.20 a year applies to shortage occupations, recent graduates and qualifying IT specialists, and the reduced route always needs agency approval.

Both figures are pegged to the pension contribution ceiling, so they reset every January. The 2025 figures were €48,300 and €43,759.80, so never rely on a number from a 2025 article when checking your offer.
sections.title: Salary thresholds for 2026

sections.content:
Your degree must be recognised in Germany. Start with the anabin database to check whether your university and degree are listed; if not, apply for a Statement of Comparability from the ZAB, which costs €208. Some shortage occupations also accept comparable professional experience instead of a formal degree.

You also need formal recognition of your foreign qualification, or a licence to practise, before the Blue Card can be issued. Only guaranteed, contractually fixed gross salary counts toward the threshold, not bonuses or variable pay.
sections.title: Degree recognition and the job offer

sections.content:
First, check your degree in anabin and secure a job offer that meets the salary threshold. Your employer may need Federal Employment Agency approval if you use the reduced threshold. Then apply at the German embassy or consulate in your country, or at the local foreigners authority if you are already in Germany.

Prepare your passport, degree documents, employment contract, and proof of health insurance. The visa fee is €75 and the residence title costs €100. Processing officially takes 4 to 12 weeks, and settlement is possible after 27 months, or 21 months with B1 German.
